articles.title: Benito Di Paula morre em São Paulo, aos 84 anos, e deixa obra singular no  samba | G1
articles.body:
O cantor, compositor e músico fluminense Benito Di Paula morre em São Paulo (SP), aos 84 anos, em decorrência de câncer — Foto: Murilo Alvesso

♬ Um dos cantores e compositores mais populares do Brasil nos anos 1970, Benito Di Paula morreu na noite deste domingo, 18 de outubro, aos 84 anos. O artista faleceu no Hospital 9 de julho, em São Paulo (SP), em decorrência de complicações de um câncer de próstata. O artista lutava contra a doença há cerca de um ano. Ainda não há informações sobre o velório e o enterro do cantor.

Cantor, compositor e músico fluminense, Benito Di Paula nasceu Uday Velloso (28 de novembro de 1941 – 18 de outubro de 2026) na cidade de Nova Friburgo (RJ) e foi criado no Rio de Janeiro (RJ). Mas o Brasil já o conheceu como Benito Di Paula a partir dos anos 1970, década em que o artista fez sucesso nacional com um samba diferente, esquema novo .

Benito Di Paula jamais se considerou um sambista da dinastia de Martinho da Vila e Paulinho da Viola, cantores e compositores que também obtiveram grande sucesso na década de 1970 no segmento do samba. Benito sempre se rotulou publicamente como sambeiro e como pianeiro .

Foi no toque percussivo do piano que Benito Di Paula fazia a própria batucada com um suingue brasileiro que, de certa forma, antecipou o pagode paulista que seria propagado nos anos 1990 por grupos como Raça Negra com arranjos cheios de teclados. E o fato é que o sambeiro pianeiro imprimiu assinatura singular na música do Brasil.

Diplomado na escola noturna das boates, território onde constatou que o manuseio das teclas do piano surtia efeito de batucada, Benito Di Paula marcou época nos palcos dos auditórios dos programas de TV com o informal visual de gala composto por anéis, casacas, colares, gravatas borboletas, pulseiras e, claro, os cabelos longos e outrora cacheados. Quem viveu no Brasil ao longo dos anos 1970 lembra da figura de Benito.

O cantor debutou no mercado fonográfico em 1967 e lançou em 1971 o primeiro álbum, “Benito Di Paula” (1971), ao qual se sucedeu o segundo, “Ela” (1972), apresentado um ano depois com o primeiro sucesso do artista, “Violão não se empresta a ninguém” (1972).

Contudo, o reinado de Benito Di Paula começou de fato em 1973 com dolente samba-canção, “Retalhos de cetim”, apresentado em single blockbuster naquele ano de 1973.

“Retalhos de cetim” foi o ponto de partida para o sucesso de obra que – calcada no mix do piano tocado pelo artista com instrumentos de percussão – rendeu sucessivos hits até 1984, mas sobretudo no período que foi de 1973 a 1977.

Nesse período, foi impossível ignorar “Charlie Brown” (1974), “Beleza que é você mulher” (1974), “Bandeira do samba” (1975), “Como dizia o mestre” (1975), “Vai ficar na saudade” (1975), “Tudo está no seu lugar” (1976), “Do jeito que a vida quer” (1976, grande samba dos versos confessionais “...É que meu samba me ajuda na vida / Minha dor vai passando esquecida”), “Assobiar e chupar cana” (1977) e “Proteção às borboletas” (1977).

Apresentadas ao longo de quatro anos, no já mencionado período de 1973 a 1977, auge da carreira de Benito, essas músicas atestaram o talento do compositor para fazer samba descolado da matriz do gênero, ainda que a assumida maior influência do sambeiro tenha sido a obra do bamba Ataulfo Alves (1909 – 1969).

Lançados em discos editados pelo cantor na gravadora Copacabana, na qual Benito permaneceu até 1980 e para a qual voltou brevemente em 1987 e em 1992, esses sucessos da década de 1970 já são suficientes para garantir a imortalidade de Benito Di Paula na galeria dos criadores da música do Brasil.

Contudo, o cantor ainda emplacou eventuais hits na primeira metade da década de 80. “Ah! Como eu amei”, música dos irmãos Jota Vellozo e Nei Vellozo, garantiu a Benito bom lugar nas playlists de 1981. Parceria de Benito com Márcio Brandão Carneiro, “Amigo do sol, amigo da lua” (1984) tocou bem nas rádios e na TV.

Tema da trilha sonora da novela “A gata comeu” (TV Globo, 1985), “Amigo do sol, amigo da lua” foi o último sucesso de Benito Di Paula, ainda que o cantor tenha continuado a lançar discos com regularidade até 1996, ano em que apresentou o álbum “Baileiro” sem repercussão.

Desde então alijado do mercado fonográfico pela máquina das gravadoras, Benito Di Paula apresentou somente mais dois álbuns com músicas inéditas, “A felicidade é nossa” (2017) e o relativamente recente “O infalível zen” (2021), disco com o qual celebrou 80 anos de vida.

Nos últimos anos, a obra inovadora de Benito Di Paula passou por processo de reavaliação e gerou tributos na área fonográfica e também no Carnaval. Em 2025, o artista foi enredo da escola de samba Águia de Ouro, uma das mais importantes do Carnaval paulistano. A agremiação desfilou com o enredo “Em Retalhos de Cetim, a Águia de Ouro do jeito que a vida quer” e com a presença do próprio Benito, emocionado, em um dos carros alegóricos.

No entanto, o aval mais importante, o do público, sempre foi dado de imediato a esse cantor, compositor e instrumentista que deixa o nome gravado na história da música popular do Brasil ao morrer a um mês de completar 85 anos.

articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Triumphs With $15M as ‘Street Fighter’ Wins Weekend
articles.summary: A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary had audiences pumped, notching 2,000 sellout screenings and becoming the highest-grossing title in two decades for a relea...
articles.body:
Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything far outpaced box office expectations in its impressive opening as Street Fighter ended up victorious over the weekend.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's three-hour documentary You Can See Everything grossed $15 million from 855 North American theaters, averaging an eye-popping $17,544 per screen. This was well beyond initial projections for the A24 release that landed the biggest opening from fewer than 1,000 locations since 2006's Borat . The film about Theranos founder Holmes' life before starting her prison sentence had the biggest documentary debut since Michael Moore's 2004 smash Fahrenheit 9/11 , surpassing more recent offerings like this year's Melania and its $7.1 million launch .

After being made in secret over three years, You Can See Everything has maintained a sense of mystery through its intriguing marketing that followed its surprise premiere at Telluride. The film enjoyed more than 2,000 sellout screenings nationwide this weekend, and videos on social media showed lines snaking through cinemas. The audience skewed young, with 70 percent under age 35 for a crowd that was 55 percent male. It will add to its theater count next weekend and continues a hot year for A24, following such previous 2026 successes as Backrooms , The Drama and The Invite.

The film's Oscar buzz is likely to increase as You Can See Everything boasts sterling word of mouth. It holds a 99 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a score of 98 from audiences, while standing as the highest-rated Letterboxd title ever at 4.8. THR critic Angie Han praised it as "smart, funny and full of surprises."

In total, the weekend's domestic box office sum stands at an estimated $101.6 million, according to Rentrak, placing it 45 percent above the equivalent 2025 weekend that saw Black Phone 2 open at No. 1 with $27.3 million. This year has reached roughly $8.2 billion domestically, putting it well ahead of last year's $6.8 billion to this point but behind the pre-pandemic level for 2019, which had hit $8.9 billion by now.

Landing on the lighter side of Paramount Pictures' projected sum, Street Fighter opened with $31 million from 3,575 North American theaters. Marking the first release in Paramount's distribution deal with Legendary, the studio had been expecting a debut in the mid-$30 millions for director Kitao Sakurai's feature adaptation of the Capcom video game. It added $20.1 million from 65 international markets. Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji and Callina Liang star in the $82 million-budgeted movie focusing on a combat tournament.

Street Fighter earned a B- CinemaScore from audiences, same as the 1994 movie of the same name that kicked off the franchise with Jean-Claude Van Damme in the lead. The new film has struggled to win over critics, holding a 41 percent approval from Rotten Tomatoes reviewers (which is an improvement on the 1994 film's 20 critics score), along with an audience score of 79. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Frank Scheck called Street Fighter a "jumbled tonal mess" and "only sporadically entertaining."

Universal Pictures' Other Mommy heads for third place with around $8.3 million, marking a decline of about 70 percent after earning a D+ CinemaScore in last weekend's debut . Jessica Chastain stars as a sinister spirit appearing in a girl's closet in Rob Savage's horror offering that heads to an estimated domestic sum of $44.8 million after opening at No. 1 a week ago.

20th Century Studios' Whalefall struggled to make a splash and is expected to reel in $8 million as it opened in 3,065 North American theaters. This is below the low double-digits that the studio was projecting for director Brian Duffield's survival thriller starring Austin Abrams as a scuba diver swallowed by a sperm whale. Earning a B CinemaScore, Whalefall carries a $60 million budget, meaning that the feature adaptation of Daniel Kraus' 2023 novel is likely to have trouble turning a profit. It added $9.5 million from 51 international markets.

Whalefall holds a 71 percent critics approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with an 81 score from audiences. THR chief film critic David Rooney wrote in his review that the movie is "just not batshit crazy enough to be much fun."

Coming in just under that on the chart is Focus Features' Sense and Sensibility , which grossed an estimated opening of $7.2 million from 2,545 North American theaters. Earning an A- CinemaScore, director Georgia Oakley's adaptation of Jane Austen's esteemed novel stars Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles in the story of the Dashwood sisters navigating life after their father's death.

Its crowd was largely female at 84 percent, with 58 percent of the audience between the ages of 18 and 34. Carrying a budget in the mid-$20 millions, Sense and Sensibility holds a 76 percent approval from Rotten Tomatoes critics and a 90 score from audiences. Rooney noted that the film "seldom steps out from the long shadow of Ang Lee's enchanting 1995 retelling."

Additionally, Netflix released buzzy Oscar contender La Bola Negra in four theaters, with this title marking the first time ever that the streamer has publicly released box office returns. The film's $69,375 per-screen average becomes the second-highest ever for a non-English language release, behind only 2019's Parasite. Starring Guitarricadelafuente and Miguel Bernardeau, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvowith's movie explores queer identity over three timelines, with critic Richard Lawson's THR review praising it as "vivid and transporting."

Likely to land just outside the top 10 is Ken Russell's The Devils , with Warner Bros. Clockwork rereleasing the controversial 1971 cult classic to the tune of $1.6 million from 350 domestic locations. Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave star in the story of a charming priest accused of witchcraft in 17th-century France.

After debuting on four screens last weekend, Bleecker Street expanded Alex Gibney's nearly four-hour documentary Musk to 472 domestic locations, as it collected $306,702 for a $650 per-screen average. THR reported over the weekend that TikTok had banned the film's advertising account.

The options heading to theaters next weekend include Clayface , Wildwood , Klara and the Sun , Ali G: Who Iz I? and Wicker .

This story was first published on Oct. 17 at 8:55 a.m.

articles.title: Cindy Crawford, Kaia Gerber Break Their Silence on Presley Gerber’s Death: “A Sweet, Beautiful Soul”
articles.summary: Crawford's son Presley died in September at age 27.
articles.body:
Cindy Crawford and Kaia Gerber are breaking their silence following the death of Presley Gerber, at age 27 last month.

Crawford took to her Instagram on Sunday to share a heartfelt tribute for her son, writing, "We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years."

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability," the model and actress continued. "We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia."

Crawford also shared a black-and-white photo of Presley and thanked artist Sebastian Faena for "capturing this beautiful image."

Kaia, who is Presley's young sister, also took to Instagram Sunday to share a lengthy tribute. "Prez, I don't have the words, and maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn't need them all along. Words fail and words subtract and words summarize and words always lack truth. And how naive of me to believe that language could transcend grief."

"I've read all of the books and I have none of the answers. My articulation is no match against this, the magnitude of losing you. I am, quite literally, down on my fucking knees," she continued. "You know how much I loved being your sister. It has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. I came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. I had more love for you than I knew what to do with. And now that it has nowhere obvious to go, I'm certain it's going to swallow me whole."

"My best buddy, my great protector, the hardest I've ever laughed and the one true love of my life — you lit all my candles and took all of my monsters away. And I love you," Kaia later added.

The Hollywood Reporter previously reported that Presley died at a rehab facility on Sept. 20, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. His official cause of death has yet to be revealed.

Presley was Crawford and Rande Gerber's eldest child, and the older brother of model-actress Kaia, who most recently appeared in Ryan Murphy's The Shards.

He began modeling as a teen, signing with IMG Models at age 15. He also worked with several brands throughout his career, including Moschino, Dolce & Gabbana and Calvin Klein, among others.

Before his death, Presley had been open about his struggles with his mental health, depression and substance abuse.

articles.title: Vidyut Jammwal's 'Street Fighter' tops box office with USD 51 million global opening; Elizabeth Holmes movie 'You Can See Everything' a hit in theaters
articles.summary: North American movie theaters were flooded with new films this weekend, including a video game reboot, a big budget survival thriller and a Jane Austen
articles.body: North American movie theaters were flooded with new films this weekend, including a video game reboot, a big budget survival thriller and a Jane Austen adaptation.Paramount's 'Street Fighter' took the first-place spot, earning USD 31 million from 3,575 theaters according to studio estimates on Sunday. The film topped the charts as expected with a USD 51 million global opening, including USD 20 million from international showings. The movie starring Callina Liang, Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji cost a reported $82 million to make, not accounting for marketing and promotion. Audiences were 69% male.'You Can See Everything' had thousands of selloutsmost of the attention and cultural discourse was elsewhere: On the nearly three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary, 'You Can See Everything'.Buzz and box office don't always line up, but 'You Can See Everything' made an extraordinary USD 15 million from only 855 screens, with over 2,000 sellout showings over the weekend, according to A24. It also had the biggest opening for a film playing on under 1,000 screens since 'Borat' opened to USD 26.5 million in 2006, and the biggest nonmusic documentary opening in two decades, since 'Fahrenheit 9/11' made nearly USD 24 million from 868 theaters. Those numbers do not account for inflation.Like other hits this year, like the Gen-Z driven 'Backrooms' and 'Obsession', ticket sales for 'You Can See Everything' were driven by a largely younger audience. Over 70% of the opening weekend crowd was under 35.The film, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, was made in secret over three years. Fielder spent over a month with the disgraced Theranos founder and her family, including two young children and partner Billy Evans, in her final days before reporting to federal prison. The reviews have been extremely positive, with 99% on Rotten Tomatoes and 99 on Metacritic. It also got an unprecedented 91% "definite recommend" from audiences, according to PostTrak exit polls.The film reportedly cost under $7 million to make and less than $10 million to market.'Street Fighter' knocks out 'Whalefall'Both 'Street Fighter' and 'You Can See Everything' may have contributed to the relative failure of 'Whalefall' this weekend. The USD 60 million survival thriller starring Austin Abrams and Josh Brolin made USD 8 million from 3,065 locations in the U.S. and Canada, despite being better reviewed than 'Street Fighter'. With USD 9.5 million from international showings, the Disney release had a USD 17.5 million global launch.'Whalefall' opened in fourth place, behind the Jessica Chastain horror 'Other Mommy'. The Universal Pictures release added USD 8.4 million in its second weekend, bringing its domestic total to USD 44.9 million.'Sense and Sensibility' off to USD 7.3 million startFifth place went to 'Sense and Sensibility', which earned an estimated USD 7.3 million from 2,545 theaters. The well-reviewed Austen adaptation starring Daisy Edgar-Jones drew a predominantly younger (58% between the ages of 14 and 18) and female crowd (84%). It also got the strongest CinemaScore of the week (A-).Warner Bros. Clockwork also released a restored presentation of Ken Russell's 1971 film 'The Devils' in 350 locations, where it made USD 1.6 million. It's the first release from the studio's specialty label.'Musk' documentary facing advertising blocks and Netflix shares box office for 'La Bola Negra'Alex Gibney's Elon Musk documentary 'Musk' also expanded to 472 screens in the U.S. and Canada, where it made USD 306,702. The film, which runs nearly four hours, has faced issues advertising on major social media platforms including X, which Musk owns, and TikTok, according to distributor Bleecker Street, which said TikTok this weekend permanently suspended the film's ad account.Netflix also shared ticket sales for the first time for the queer Spanish epic 'La Bola Negra', which made USD 277,500 from four locations this weekend. The streamer has not historically reported box office for its theatrical releases, but this film is breaking new ground as it's being positioned as a possible best picture contender. It will be in theaters for 47 days before it will be available to watch on Netflix.According to Rentrak, the weekend overall generated about USD 101.6 million in ticket sales, up 45% from the same weekend last year. The year to date stands at USD 8.2 billion, which is up almost 20% from 2025.Top 10 movies at the domestic box officeWith final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak:1. articles.title: Documentário de Brasília mostra espera de mulheres com câncer de mama por tratamento no SUS | G1
articles.standfirst: Filme Esse Outubro Não É Rosa será exibido na quinta-feira (22), no Cine Brasília, com debate sobre filas de regulação e acesso à saúde.
articles.summary: Filme Esse Outubro Não É Rosa será exibido na quinta-feira (22), no Cine Brasília, com debate sobre filas de regulação e acesso à saúde.
articles.body:
Documentário 'Esse Outubro Não É Rosa' será exibido na quinta-feira (22), às 19h, no Cine Brasília. — Foto: Divulgação

Um documentário produzido em Brasília promete mostrar a realidade de mulheres com câncer de mama que enfrentam a demora para conseguir exames, diagnósticos e tratamentos pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

O longa Esse Outubro Não É Rosa , dirigido por Luciana Salvatore, será exibido na quinta-feira (22), às 19h, no Cine Brasília, na Asa Sul.

Após a sessão, haverá um debate com a diretora, personagens do filme, especialistas e profissionais de saúde . A recepção ao público e o coquetel começam às 18h.

Lançado em outubro de 2025, o documentário aborda as dificuldades enfrentadas por pacientes que precisam lidar com a doença enquanto aguardam atendimento na rede pública. A produção também propõe uma reflexão sobre as desigualdades no acesso à saúde e os impactos da demora no tratamento.

Histórias de mulheres que enfrentam o câncer

O documentário acompanha Fátima e Rafaella, duas mulheres que sobreviveram ao câncer de mama e que, após a recidiva da doença, voltaram a enfrentar os desafios do tratamento.

Enquanto aguardam exames, diagnósticos e procedimentos, as protagonistas lidam com a incerteza e com a urgência de iniciar o atendimento. As histórias expõem as dificuldades de quem depende da rede pública de saúde para dar continuidade ao tratamento.

Para Grace Justa, diretora do Instituto de Desenvolvimento Humano Umanizzare, parceiro da produção, o filme busca dar visibilidade às falhas no atendimento e estimular o debate sobre as filas de regulação.

Segundo Grace, o documentário também aborda a responsabilidade coletiva diante dos problemas estruturais que dificultam o acesso ao atendimento.

O longa conquistou cinco prêmios internacionais. Entre eles estão o de Melhor Filme Independente no Cannes Arts Film Fest; os de Melhor Filme de Longa-Metragem e Melhor Direção de Longa-Metragem, para Luciana Salvatore, no Indiana Independent Film Festival; o de Melhor Narrativa Feminina de Longa-Metragem no Calgary Independent Film Festival; e o de Melhor Longa-Metragem sobre Empoderamento Feminino no London Women Film Festival.

articles.title: 'Jailer 2' box office collection day 4: Rajinikanth, Mohanlal, Nelson Dilipkumar film sees Sunday jump; earns Rs 55.85 cr in India; worldwide gross hits Rs 424.25 cr
articles.summary: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' continued its strong box office run on Sunday, October 18, collecting Rs 55.85 cr net in India on its fourth day.
articles.body: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' continued its strong box office run on Sunday, October 18, collecting Rs 55.85 cr net in India on its fourth day. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, the action entertainer recorded an overall occupancy of 62% across 15,473 shows. According to Sacnilk, the film's worldwide gross collection has reached Rs 424.25 cr, including earnings from domestic and overseas markets.Jailer 2 ReviewThe fourth-day collection also marks an 18.2% increase over Saturday's India net collection of Rs 47.25 cr. With this, the film's cumulative India net collection stands at Rs 199.90 cr, while its domestic gross has reached Rs 234.25 cr. The film has also crossed the Rs 150 cr net collection milestone in India. 'Jailer 2' box office collection day-wise'Jailer 2' began its theatrical run with Rs 59.70 cr net in India on Thursday, October 15. The film recorded 55.4% occupancy across 16,599 shows. On Friday, October 16, collections dropped to Rs 37.10 cr from 13,157 shows, with occupancy at 48.2%.The Rajinikanth-starrer recovered on Saturday, October 17, earning Rs 47.25 cr from 14,604 shows at 53.9% occupancy. Sunday brought another increase, with collections reaching Rs 55.85 cr and occupancy rising to 62%. The film recorded 3,687,269 footfalls on Day 4, taking its total footfalls over four days to 13,021,526.The Tamil version remained the biggest contributor on Sunday, earning Rs 39.95 cr net from 8,173 shows at 80% occupancy. The Telugu version collected Rs 9.50 cr across 2,234 shows, registering 64.3% occupancy. The Hindi version added Rs 5.75 cr from 4,902 shows at 31% occupancy, while the Kannada version earned Rs 0.65 cr across 164 shows, with occupancy at 61%.The Tamil version recorded 82.58% overall occupancy in 2D screenings. Morning shows registered 67.08%, while afternoon, evening and night screenings recorded 87.08%, 88.77% and 87.38%, respectively.The Hindi version registered 44.40% overall occupancy, with morning shows at 28.58%, afternoon screenings at 49.83%, evening shows at 47.83% and night screenings at 46%. Meanwhile, the Telugu version recorded 61.81% overall occupancy. Its morning shows registered 41.92%, followed by 70.58% in the afternoon, 71.83% in the evening and 62.92% at night.Overseas collection pushes worldwide total past Rs 424 cr'Jailer 2' collected Rs 40 cr from overseas markets on Day 4, taking its cumulative overseas gross to Rs 190 cr. Combined with its India gross of Rs 234.25 cr, the film's worldwide gross has reached Rs 424.25 cr.Shamna Kasim expresses gratitude to Rajinikanth and teamMeanwhile, actor Shamna Kasim has thanked audiences for their response to her dance appearance in 'Jailer 2'. She also expressed gratitude to director Nelson Dilipkumar, producer Kalanithi Maran and composer Anirudh Ravichander for giving her the opportunity to be part of the film.In a social media video, Shamna Kasim spoke about sharing screen space with Rajinikanth, whom she has admired for years. She also mentioned 'Padayappa' as one of her favorite films featuring the veteran actor."Everyone would like to share screen space with a style icon such as Rajinikanth sir. I never thought that I would have that opportunity," Shamna said. 'Jailer 2' cast and special appearancesRajinikanth returns as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian in the sequel. The supporting cast includes S.J. Suryah as Bodhi Kalpak, Mithun Chakraborty as Chakri, Suraj Venjaramoodu as Dileep, Ramya Krishnan, Vidya Balan and Yogi Babu. articles.title: Tiger Shroff covers face, reaches home under police protection after Juhu firing; tape on hand draws attention
articles.summary: Tiger Shroff was moved to safety under police protection after shots were fired in Mumbai’s Juhu on Sunday, October 18, 2026.
articles.body: Tiger Shroff was moved to safety under police protection after shots were fired in Mumbai’s Juhu on Sunday, October 18, 2026. Social media videos show the actor in a vehicle, flanked by security. Though tape on his hand drew attention online, police confirmed he sustained no bullet injuries.Videos show Tiger Shroff leaving under police escortAn Instagram video posted by the paparazzi shows Tiger sitting in a vehicle while police officers take him away from the scene. According to the account, the Mumbai Police provided the actor with protection and escorted him to his home. articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing incident: Ahsaas Channa calls it scary; Amol Parashar says, ‘Whoever has broken the law should be caught and punished’
articles.summary: Several actors have expressed shock after shots were fired at Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai, raising concerns about safety in the entertainment industry.
articles.body: Several actors have expressed shock after shots were fired at Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai, raising concerns about safety in the entertainment industry. Ahsaas Channa, Nishant Malkani, Amol Parashar, Apoorva Arora, Alam Khan and Riva Arora reacted to the incident on Sunday. While Tiger Shroff escaped without gunshot injuries, two people were hurt in the firing, according to the police, as reported by ANI.Ahsaas Channa hopes Tiger Shroff remains safeAhsaas Channa said she was relieved that Tiger Shroff had escaped unharmed but remained concerned about his safety. She also hoped he would remain safe in the future."I am very, very happy that he is safe. But I am also a little scared for him. I hope he is okay and even in the future he is always safe," she told ANI. Ahsaas Channa said more information was needed before drawing conclusions about the incident or connecting it to the city."I don't think that this is related to the city. I think we need to know more about it and need more information, only then can we comment on it," she added.She also urged people to take precautions and expressed hope that the police would respond appropriately. "I think everyone should take very careful measures. I hope the police is cooperating," she said.Nishant Malkani and Amol Parashar reactNishant Malkani said he was unaware of the shooting until he was asked about it. He planned to contact Tiger Shroff to check on his well-being."It's very shocking news. I didn't know about it. I'll check and I'll call him," Nishant Malkani said. He expressed sadness over the incident and said such events should not happen."It's a sad thing. What can we say? Such things should not happen, that's it," he added.Amol Parashar described the incident as frightening and said news of violence often worries actors' families. He recalled how his parents would contact him to check where he was whenever they heard similar reports."Such things are shocking and scary too. I think everyone gets scared. My parents, whenever they hear this news, will first call or message and ask where I am and whether I am outside," he said.Amol Parashar also called for strict action against anyone found guilty, saying punishment could help prevent further crimes."Whoever has broken the law, whoever has done something wrong, should be caught and punished. The way to reduce crime is to catch criminals and punish them. If they don't get punished, other people will also get encouragement to do wrong things," he said.Apoorva Arora and Alam Khan express concernApoorva Arora said she had only recently heard about the incident and hoped everyone involved was safe. She also expressed hope that justice would be served."I actually just found out inside and it's very unfortunate that this happened. I hope everything is okay and everyone is okay. I haven't seen the news yet, but someone informed me about this. It's very, very unfortunate that in a city like this, this is happening. I hope there is justice," Apoorva Arora said in an interaction with ANI.She added that the incident was difficult to process but expressed faith in Mumbai's safety and administration."It's very scary, honestly. There are no words to genuinely process it because I have just found out. I would like to believe that Mumbai city is still safe and will remain safe, thanks to the Mumbai Police and administration here," she said.Alam Khan also said he was shocked by the news and did not know what had led to the shooting."I just saw the news. In fact, it was very shocking. I really don't know what the reason could be," he said.Riva Arora calls the incident frighteningRiva Arora said the shooting was frightening and hoped Tiger Shroff was safe. She noted that such incidents could leave people feeling vulnerable."Oh my God. It's scary actually. Sometimes it gets so scary for an actor, for everybody. Suddenly, you don't know when what will happen. I really hope he is okay," she said.Questioning the reasons behind such acts, Riva Arora said they could cause significant emotional distress."I don't know. I just don't understand what people get by doing all this. It's very scary for somebody also to experience this and it gives you a different level of trauma," she said. She also described the situation as "crazy" and difficult to comprehend.Mumbai Police deploy 15 teams for investigationReportedly, the Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the firing. According to the police, three to four rounds were fired at Tiger Shroff's car as he was leaving a ground where a large crowd had gathered to see him. The shots were reportedly fired from within the crowd.Tiger Shroff did not sustain any gunshot injuries. However, two people were injured, including his driver, Firdaus, who suffered a gunshot wound to his left arm. The police are continuing their investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. articles.title: Gig-going York artist draws 'crazy crowds'from mosh pit
articles.summary: Sam Joesbury draws pictures of crowds at concerts while dancing in the mosh pit himself.
articles.body:
Most people can't even hold a drink when they're among the crowd at the front of a gig - but for Yorkshire artist Sam Joesbury, being thrown around in the mosh pit is where he creates his best work.

The 22-year-old, from York, started drawing at concerts last year, and what started as a hobby has led to him sketching at several gigs a week, sharing his work on social media and gaining thousands of fans online.

"It was all a bit of a joke and a laugh until I realised, no one else is doing this and it is actually really fun," he said.

"Some of the favourite bands I've drawn live include Basht, who I am on tour with now, but also Turnstile live at the Piece Hall, Fontaines D.C. at Leeds Festival and Kneecap, who were just crazy."

He added: "I really love getting involved with some of the most crazy crowds. It really brings out the fact that this is about getting involved, getting my hands dirty and getting into the most lively atmosphere that I possibly can."

Sam, who has a degree in Fine Art from Lancaster University, said he started sketching the crowds in his notebook before the concerts began - but soon realised the real magic was in capturing the energy of the night.

He said: "After the first few drawings that were done beforehand, I got caught out by one of the bands and I decided it's probably time to do it for real.

"It was a question of, is this even good, is it worth it, am I stressing myself out by trying to make the drawing look good?

"Then I realised this is about having fun, and when I stopped worrying I started focussing on having the drawing replicate the experience that I was having.

"That's when I started going a bit bonkers and getting [into] mosh pits and rowdy crowds.

"That's when the drawings came to life and became a document of the experience rather than just a drawing of a band on an occasion."

His first drawing was at a Drake concert, but he has since drawn the Kaiser Chiefs, A$AP Rocky, The K's and Keo.

The artist, who has more than 20,000 followers on Instagram, said he started drawing because he had been working on hyperrealism for years.

The genre includes drawings which are lifelike and high resolution, almost like a photograph.

He also loves drawing at gigs to shine a light on new music and grassroots venues - and while he loves hard rock, metal and rap, he credits his sister Grace with the indie music knowledge that helps him find new crowds to draw.

"I am not just thinking about what is going to do well for me, I love shedding light on the bands, but my sister is all about shedding light onto every band," he said.

"My sister Grace, you will find her at any small gig, her indie knowledge is off the chart."

Grace, a student at university in Leeds, is often the one filming Sam as he works.

"There is not much representation for these smaller indie bands," he said.

"All they have to do is give me the opportunity to come and draw them, and it is a bit of promo and a bit of fun for me.

"It is impossible to do an accurate drawing in a mosh pit so people say why bother doing it?

"Well it's not about it looking how it is meant to look, it is about doing something unique and capturing the energy and atmosphere and providing something for the fans, and for the band, as a memento for that specific occasion.

"It is capturing that unique venue, with that specific crowd and that specific set list, where there is a different energy and it is different every time."

articles.body: Shatrughan Sinha has reacted to the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai's Juhu area, calling it "shocking" and raising concerns over the safety of the actor and his family.Sinha, in a post on X, spoke about the incident, in which Tiger reportedly escaped without serious injuries while his driver was injured. Yesterday's shocking, worrying attacks, threats, targeting & firing on most loved star @TIGERSHROFF worthy son of the most worthy father @bindasbhidu. According to the police, unidentified individuals opened fire as Tiger was leaving a football club in his car at around 7 pm.A case has been registered against three unidentified individuals under Sections 109(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act.Two people, including Tiger's driver, were injured in the incident. articles.summary: Emraan Hashmi’s upcoming action thriller ‘Gunmaaster G9’ has prompted renewed attention to stunt safety after an SUV came loose from its rigging during a
articles.body: Emraan Hashmi’s upcoming action thriller ‘Gunmaaster G9’ has prompted renewed attention to stunt safety after an SUV came loose from its rigging during a climax shoot in Bengaluru on October 13, narrowly missing a passing van. The incident left the actor and others in the frame unharmed but led the makers to review their arrangements and reinforce safety checks before every stunt. Directed by Aditya Datt, the film also stars Genelia Deshmukh and is scheduled to release on November 27.Emraan Hashmi’s ‘Gunmaaster G9’ shoot scare prompts stricter safety checksThe climax shoot of ‘Gunmaaster G9’ turned into a wake-up call for the film’s team, highlighting the risks involved in staging elaborate action sequences. On October 13, Emraan Hashmi was filming a sequence involving an SUV and a fleet of cars in Bengaluru when the SUV came loose from its rigging and nearly crashed into a van passing nearby.Fortunately, Hashmi and the others in the frame escaped without injuries. However, the incident underscored the importance of meticulous planning and coordination when executing potentially dangerous stunts.Speaking to Mid-Day, producer Deepak Mukut emphasised that the responsibility of delivering large-scale action on screen must go hand in hand with protecting everyone working on the film.“Action cinema demands a certain physicality and scale, and we want to bring that experience to the big screen. But our responsibility towards the people working on the film is equally important. The safety of our actors, technicians, and crew must always remain paramount. Every action sequence requires careful planning and coordination, and we take that responsibility seriously,” he said.‘Gunmaaster G9’ makers review stunt arrangements after SUV comes looseA video from the set that surfaced online showed crew members gathered around the stunt setup as a countdown was called for the shot. Moments later, the SUV came dangerously close to landing on the passing van, raising concerns about the precautions required for such sequences.Following the incident, director Aditya Datt, Mukut and the action team reportedly reviewed the arrangements on set. According to a source quoted by the publication, the team is reinforcing the checks required before attempting similar stunts.“Following the incident, we are reinforcing the checks required before any such stunt is attempted. It includes checking all securing points and ensuring that the action team and crew are aligned on movement, positioning, and clearance zones. We want to get a sense of what additional precautions may be required before proceeding with similar shots,” the source said.The review focuses on securing points, movement coordination, crew positioning and clearance zones to minimise risks during action sequences. articles.title: Richard Gere, de 77 años, sobre Europa: "Entienden la vida de una manera diferente a como lo hacemos en Estados Unidos"
articles.standfirst: El protagonista de Pretty Woman destaca la alegría y menor tensión de los españoles
articles.summary: El protagonista de Pretty Woman destaca la alegría y menor tensión de los españoles
articles.body: El reconocido actor Richard Gere inició hace más de un año su nueva vida en España junto a su esposa, Alejandra Silva. Durante su asistencia a un evento en la ciudad de Nueva York, el protagonista de grandes éxitos cinematográficos compartió con la revista 'People' los motivos que hacen de su nuevo hogar un lugar excepcional, destacando el bienestar de su familia y el carácter único de la cultura local. El intérprete entonces explicó que el pilar fundamental de esta mudanza es la felicidad de su pareja, subrayando el entorno afectivo con el que cuenta allí. "Mi esposa es muy feliz en España, y esa es la mejor parte", confesó, añadiendo que "tiene una familia maravillosa y amigos maravillosos". Asimismo, el actor alabó el temperamento de la sociedad española frente al ritmo vertiginoso de Norteamérica: "La cultura española tiene una alegría muy abierta", y añadió que los españoles son "muy cálidos, muy abiertos y mucho menos estresados que lo que se encuentra aquí en Estados Unidos". Profundizando en su experiencia europea, Gere comparó esta atmósfera con la de otras regiones del continente y apuntó una diferencia cultural clave: "Es un lugar muy feliz. Como los italianos. Es decir, estar en Italia, estar en España, implica tratar con culturas latinas que entienden la vida de una manera diferente a como lo hacemos aquí". No obstante, reconoció que todavía echa de menos ciertos aspectos de su rutina anterior en Nueva York, concretamente la "energía" de la gran manzana, afirmando que "claro que es muy adictiva". Esta mudanza familiar ha supuesto un profundo cambio vital para el actor, quien previamente ya había comentado a la revista Elle España que ha hallado una nueva plenitud tras trasladarse al viejo continente con su esposa y sus hijos. "Nos ven en nuestro mejor momento. Estamos más felices que nunca", declaró, recalcando que "[Alejandra], porque está en casa, y yo, porque si ella es feliz, yo soy feliz". Más allá de su dinámica familiar, el matrimonio comparte una fuerte complicidad basada en valores comunes y proyectos medioambientales y solidarios. El actor reflexionó sobre la importancia de la humildad en su labor humanitaria, afirmando que "todos podemos minimizar este sentido del ego, del yo. Y es entonces cuando se produce el verdadero cambio". Del mismo modo, ensalzó las virtudes personales de su compañera de vida: "Mi esposa destaca por su mentalidad abierta y su sincero sentido de gratitud". Por su parte, Alejandra Silva también ha manifestado en diversas ocasiones la gran conexión que mantiene con el intérprete desde que se conocieron en Italia en el año 2014. Para describir su historia de amor, la empresaria señaló que son "almas gemelas", agregando que comparten la misma visión del mundo y que su sólido vínculo parece estar guiado por el destino y unos valores inquebrantables.

articles.title: Ravi Kishan reacts to Tiger Shroff firing incident; calls it a matter of concern; expresses faith in Maharashtra Police
articles.summary: Actor Ravi Kishan has expressed shock over the firing incident involving Bollywood star Tiger Shroff.
articles.body: Actor Ravi Kishan has expressed shock over the firing incident involving Bollywood star Tiger Shroff.Speaking to the media at Patna airport, Ravi condemned the shocking incident, calling it a matter of concern and expressing hope that the Mumbai Police would soon track down the culprits."Bhaut dukhad hua...chinta ka vishay hai. (It is a matter of great concern and a matter for investigation). We have full faith in the Maharashtra Police. An investigation will take place, and those found guilty will receive the harshest possible punishment. It is a deeply concerning and serious matter. Tiger is a very innocent person. I pray to Mahadev and Mata Rani to protect him. The Maharashtra Police and the Maharashtra government are leaving no stone unturned. Very soon, all those responsible will be caught and given the severest punishment," he said.According to Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Mohit Garg, Tiger Shroff narrowly escaped injury after unidentified individuals opened fire as he was leaving the football club in his car at around 7 pm on Sunday. Two people, including the actor's driver, sustained injuries in the incident that happened in Mumbai's Juhu area.The driver was reportedly struck by bullets, while the actor escaped without any gunshot injuries.After news emerged that the actor was targeted in a shooting, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited his residence on Sunday night to enquire about his well-being and to assure him of the state government's support.Photographs from Tiger Shroff's residence showed the actor with dressings on his shoulder and chest and a bandage on his right arm as he interacted with Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Tiger's mother, Ayesha Shroff, was also present during the meeting.After meeting the actor, Shinde spoke to reporters and condemned the firing incident. He said Tiger had sustained injuries to his hand caused by "gunpowder and shards of glass" and assured the family that the state government would take the necessary steps to ensure their safety."This is a major incident... five rounds were fired, but fortunately, he was safe. His driver sustained injuries, and the incident is condemnable. I met with the actor; he has injuries on his left hand caused by gunpowder and shards of glass. Both he and his mother are quite shaken... I have assured them that the state government stands with them in the face of the open threats being directed at public figures... No form of threat will be tolerated. Such gang wars were quite common in the 90s, but the Mumbai Police put an end to them in 1995... These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," Shinde said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Salman Khan’s Bandra home gets additional security; Mumbai Crime Branch tracks suspects to Gujarat
articles.summary: Mumbai Police have reportedly strengthened security outside Salman Khan’s Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra following the firing incident involving
articles.body: Mumbai Police have reportedly strengthened security outside Salman Khan’s Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra following the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff’s car in Juhu on Sunday evening. Visuals shared by ANI showed police personnel wearing bulletproof jackets and police vehicles stationed outside the actor’s home.The shooting reportedly occurred around 7 pm when Tiger Shroff was leaving a football club in Juhu. Three unidentified motorcycle-borne men allegedly opened fire at his vehicle. The actor escaped direct gunshot injuries, but his driver was injured. Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg confirmed that the vehicle was targeted as Tiger was leaving the club.Crime Branch expands search to GujaratReports say that the Mumbai Police Crime Branch has extended its investigation to Gujarat to track down the suspected attackers. Investigators suspect the men had monitored Tiger Shroff’s movements before the shooting. According to the reports, they were aware of his regular Sunday visits to the football ground and may have conducted a recce of the area.The suspects allegedly fled along SV Road through Vile Parle and Andheri after the incident. They reportedly abandoned their motorcycle near Andheri West railway station before boarding a train towards Borivali. Police suspect they later crossed into Gujarat to evade arrest. Three to four Crime Branch teams are conducting raids at suspected locations.An FIR has been registered against three unidentified persons under Sections 109(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act. The investigation remains underway.Eknath Shinde visits Tiger ShroffMaharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Tiger Shroff’s residence on Sunday night to meet the actor and his mother, Ayesha Shroff. Talking to the media, he said Tiger had sustained injuries to his left hand from gunpowder and glass fragments. The incident had also left the actor and his mother shaken.Assuring them of the state government’s support, Eknath Shinde said, "Strict action will be taken, and threats against public figures will not be tolerated."Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also contacted the Mumbai Police Commissioner to discuss the incident. He directed the police chief to investigate the shooting immediately and take strict action against those responsible. Mumbai Police have formed 15 special teams to pursue the case.FWICE condemns firing incidentThe Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) has condemned the attack and demanded better security for Tiger Shroff and his family. The organisation expressed concern over repeated incidents involving prominent members of the film industry, referring to the earlier firing incident involving filmmaker Rohit Shetty.In its statement, FWICE said, "Such acts of violence and intimidation are completely unacceptable and raise serious concerns about the safety and security of personalities associated with the Indian film industry. It is deeply disturbing that this is the second such incident involving a prominent personality from the film industry, following the earlier firing incident involving renowned filmmaker Mr. Rohit Shetty. The recurrence of such incidents is a matter of grave concern and calls for immediate, decisive and effective action by the concerned authorities."The organisation called for a thorough investigation and urged the Maharashtra government and police to improve safety measures.Ravi Kishan reacts to the shootingActor and politician Ravi Kishan has also expressed concern over the incident. Speaking to reporters at Patna airport, he said he trusted the Maharashtra Police to identify the culprits and ensure they received severe punishment."Bhaut dukhad hua...chinta ka vishay hai. (It is a matter of great concern and a matter for investigation). We have full faith in the Maharashtra Police. An investigation will take place, and those found guilty will receive the harshest possible punishment. It is a deeply concerning and serious matter. Tiger is a very innocent person. I pray to Mahadev and Mata Rani to protect him. The Maharashtra Police and the Maharashtra government are leaving no stone unturned. Very soon, all those responsible will be caught and given the severest punishment," he said, as quoted by ANI.Meanwhile, Tiger Shroff’s mother, Ayesha Shroff, shared her reaction to the incident with India Today. Asked whether her son was doing well, she replied, "God is great."The Lawrence Bishnoi gang reportedly claimed responsibility for the shooting in a social media post hours after the incident. articles.summary: Filmmaker Kuku Kohli, husband of veteran Bollywood actress Aruna Irani, passed away on August 25, 2026, after suffering a heart attack. He was 77.
articles.body: Filmmaker Kuku Kohli, husband of veteran Bollywood actress Aruna Irani, passed away on August 25, 2026, after suffering a heart attack. He was 77. Two months later, Aruna shared that she is back at work and thanked her fans for their support through this painful period.Aruna Irani thanks fans in an emotional videoAruna posted an emotional video on Instagram on Sunday to thank fans for the love and support they showed her after Kuku’s passing. In the video, she said, “After Kuku Ji’s death, for the love you all gave me and supported me, I am truly grateful. I couldn’t believe that in my tough times you guys stood by me. It’s because of your love and support that I am standing in front of you and am able to resume work again. Asha karti hoon ki aap sab, meri zindagi ki aakhri saas tak yun hi mere saath rahenge (I hope you guys will stand by me like this till my last breath).”Kuku Kohli is taken ill and then suffers a sudden heart attackKuku Kohli, the filmmaker who introduced Ajay Devgn to audiences with 'Phool Aur Kaante', passed away at 77. He had been taken to Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital on August 24 after feeling unwell. Speaking to India Today, Aruna Irani’s brother, Balraj Irani, said, “He (Kuku) was absolutely fine, and then this evening he suffered a massive heart attack. He was talking to us and just collapsed.”Though doctors tried to revive him, Kuku Kohli was pronounced dead at about 5 pm on August 25. His last rites were performed around noon the next day, August 26. His wife, veteran actress Aruna Irani, looked visibly emotional as she said her final goodbye, joined by relatives from both the Irani and Kohli families. articles.title: Cindy Crawford breaks her silence on the death of her son, Presley Gerber: ‘Til we meet again our sweet boy’
articles.summary: Cindy Crawford is paying tribute to her son, Presley Gerber, who died in September.
articles.body: Cindy Crawford is paying tribute to her son, Presley Gerber, who died in September. For the first time since his death, Crawford addressed the tragedy in an Instagram post shared Sunday. The mom of two wrote that the family is “beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother.” “We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever,” she wrote in the Instagram post. “We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.” Supermodel Crawford and her husband, businessman Rande Gerber, also have a daughter, model and actor Kaia Gerber, who is 25. Presley Gerber died Sept. 20 at a rehabilitation facility, according to the Los Angeles County medical examiner. The records show that the cause of death is pending additional investigation. No further details were provided. In her post, Crawford thanked those who showed the family support amid the difficult time. “We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain,” she wrote. She concluded the post with a sweet message to her late son. “Til we meet again our sweet boy,” Crawford wrote. “We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia” Kaia Gerber also posted a tribute to her brother on Instagram the same day. In her post, she wrote to “prez” about “how much I loved being your sister.” “It has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. i came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you,” she wrote in a long, open letter to her brother. “i had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole.” In the Instagram post, she also shared a sweet throwback video of the siblings as kids, hugging and dancing together, along with a few old pictures. “I am learning how to love you when i cannot see you. how to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you,” Kaia Gerber wrote in the heartbreaking post. “How to be your sister in a world that I can’t reach for you in. i don’t know how to do that yet.” She also seemingly referenced physicist Richard Feynman’s famous letter to his late wife. “My darling brother, i do adore you,” Kaia Gerber wrote. “i love my brother. my brother is dead. and this party sucks so bad without you, prez.” Hours before authorities found him unresponsive, Presley Gerber had checked into rehab facility Resolutions Living of Santa Monica, a law enforcement source told NBC News. His death is being investigated as a suspected overdose, police have said. Presley Gerber has been open about his struggles with depression and addiction in the past. In June, he took part in a panel discussion about mental health, according to People magazine. It would be his final public appearance. “The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” he told the audience.

articles.title: Charlie Cox on how his son reacted to the news of ‘Daredevil: Born Again’ ending for good: ‘I’m preparing myself. He’s devastated’
articles.summary: Charlie Cox shares his son's emotional response to the cancellation of 'Daredevil: Born Again,' highlighting the impact of the superhero role on their lives.
articles.body: 43-year-old actor Charlie Cox, who brought the character Daredevil to life, opened up about how his son reacted to the show’s ending. Starring in ‘Daredevil: Born Again,' Cox opened up about how he knew that saying goodbye to the character would be hard for him; however, he was left in a state of shock over the reaction his six-year-old son had to the news.Charlie Cox on how his son reacted to finding out that ‘Daredevil: Born Again’ will not come backWhile attending the New York Comic Con earlier this month, Cox opened up about the beloved show’s ending and how he had a hard time dealing with accepting the fact that ‘Daredevil: Born Again’ is ending. Talking to PEOPLE, he shared that his son also had quite a strong reaction to the entire thing.“I don’t think I am prepared for it. It’s been 12 years of my life. I think it’s very likely that at the end of my career, whenever that is, this character will be the most important to me. I don’t know if you can prepare yourself for that. I’m trying to prepare my son for it more than I’m preparing myself. He’s devastated," he commented. He also commented on how his son was only just coming to terms with the fact that his father was playing the role of a superhero.He added, “He’s 6. So he’s just coming on to the ‘my dad’s a superhero’ kind of stuff. When I told him, the color drained from his face. It didn’t occur to me that he’d be so impacted by it, so it’s very sweet.”Charlie Cox on how it feels for him to transition out of the superhero roleDuring the interview, he also talked about how the transition and the show’s ending feel for him, adding, “I think it’s going to be weird. But at the moment, I’m just so grateful for the time that we’ve had, all the stories we’ve got to tell, and all the hours and hours. I think I’ve played Daredevil for 70 hours or something crazy. It has been such a gift and the great honor of my career.”He also talked about how the show changed his life and how he met his wife, Samantha Thomas, on the first day of filming for 'Daredevil,' and everything has been going great for them since then. Thompson and Cox have been together for 12 years now. He then concluded, “It’s been an absolute journey.”Charlie Cox has played Daredevil for 11 years, starting in 2015, when the first OTT series, 'Daredevil,' was released. He also appeared in ‘The Defenders’ and had brief cameo appearances in ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ and ‘She-Hulk: Attorney at Law.’

articles.title: You Can See Everything documentary stuns with huge box office debut
articles.summary: It shows fraudster Elizabeth Holmes invite a sceptical film into her home before she's sent to prison.
articles.body:
A three-hour documentary on the tech fraudster Elizabeth Holmes has raked in a whopping $15 million (£11.25m) on its box office debut, despite a limited run at 855 screens across the US and Canada.

The eagerly anticipated A24 film, titled You Can See Everything, was co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim.

It finds Holmes at her home in 2023 during the month before she began an 11-year prison sentence.

US publication Deadline has described it as "easily the second best opening ever for a documentary at the box office after 2004s Fahrenheit 9/11", Michael Moore's movie about the US's 2003 invasion of Iraq.

Ticket sales at the box office were enough for second place behind Paramount's new video game adaptation, Street Fighter, which opened to $31 million in North America and $51.1 million globally.

You Can See Everything also secured the largest debut for any film playing on under 1,000 screens since 2006's Borat, which scored $26 million.

Holmes was convicted of defrauding investors in her medical testing company Theranos, fuelling a media circus that has been chronicled in books, podcasts and the mini-series The Dropout, starring Amanda Seyfried.

In You Can See Everything, comedian Fielder - known for shows including The Rehearsal and The Curse - places himself inside the action, once again blurring the lines between documentary, social experiment and prank show.

We see notorious Silicon Valley founder Holmes invite a sceptical film crew to document her every move, thirty-four days before she's sent to prison.

The first teaser trailer dropped last month, right after the film's surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado.

It went viral and launched many online memes of Holmes unblinkingly asking Fielder: "Why would I deceive you?"

The stranger-than-fiction documentary has garnered rave reviews and is already being talked about as an Oscar contender as we head into awards season.

Remarkable for a documentary - that isn't based on a live music event - produced in secret over three years which no-one really knew about until recently.

The Guardian awarded the film five stars , calling it "a modern masterpiece of deceit", stressing how "TV's grand illusionist meets his match when he moves in with Theranos founder and her family".

The Financial Times also offered five stars describing documentary as "a mind-bending revelation".

The New York Times noted how it sees Holmes and Fielder "joust in a dizzying movie about truth, reality and the contours of knowledge".

The buzz around the film is likely to see it be in the running, at least, for a nomination for best documentary feature at next year's Academy Awards, though no documentary has ever been nominated for the main prize of best picture.

articles.title: 'You Can See Everything' Review: The buzzy Elizabeth Holmes documentary is worth the hype
articles.summary: Fox News Digital reviews A24's new documentary "You Can See Everything" featuring disgraced Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim.
articles.body: The best documentaries don't feel like documentaries. They have a connotation of being educational, but even career documentarians will tell you that all they're doing is telling a story just like any other film. Well, A24's "You Can See Everything" is not like any other film, nor is it like any other documentary. Comedian Nathan Fielder shocked the internet during the festival circuit earlier this year when he unveiled a documentary he spent three years developing featuring Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced Theranos founder who granted him unfettered access in the 34 days leading up to her 11-year prison sentence in 2023. ‘WHALEFALL’ REVIEW: AUSTIN ABRAMS IS SWALLOWED BY A SPERM WHALE IN IMMERSIVE SURVIVAL DRAMA You likely know the story already: Holmes became a media darling in the mid-2010s as her company had allegedly developed a medical device that can detect virtually all diseases from a single drop of blood. However, investigative reporting by The Wall Street Journal led to her downfall and she was ultimately found guilty of defrauding investors in 2022. Having lived in obscurity since the collapse of Theranos, Holmes providing unprecedented access to Fielder and co-director Lance Oppenheim certainly turned heads. Fielder serves as our on-camera shepherd, spending intimate moments with her, her husband Billy Evans and their two infant children. He isn't shy about expressing his skepticism towards Holmes and Evans as she maintains her innocence while the two of them are in the early stages of scheming a major comeback for what can be dubbed "Theranos 2.0." Both Fielder and the audience alike stare into Holmes' big blue eyes above her porcelain red cheeks, hoping to read between the lines of whether she's being as authentic as she claims to be or if she's the cunning manipulator the world believes she is. ‘THE SOCIAL RECKONING’ REVIEW: ZUCKERBERG, FACEBOOK ARE THE ENEMY IN PREACHY SLOP DISGUISED AS JOURNO DRAMA What's remarkable about "You Can See Everything" is how it becomes increasingly indiscernible on who we can really trust as the documentary progresses. Her husband is a peculiar character in his own right, and we begin to suspect his motives. We even start to question the filmmakers behind the documentary at one point, thanks in part to Fielder and Oppenheim pulling back the curtain. A fun mystery thriller develops in the process. While not notorious like Holmes, Fielder made a name for himself as the host of Comedy Central's "Nathan For You" and HBO's "The Rehearsal," both of which are part comedies, part docuseries. For comedic effect, Fielder often blurs the lines of what documentaries are supposed to do. So the strange twist and turns "You Can See Everything" takes in the second act may not exactly shock those who are familiar with his work, but the direction it goes is spellbinding nonetheless. Fielder is as awkward as he is hilarious, and the way he often uses bluntness to seek the truth is amusing. Despite the nearly three-hour runtime, it doesn't drag thanks to editor Adam Locke-Norton. The cinematography by David Bolen and the score from composer Ari Balouzian (both of whom also worked on Oppenheim's "Primetime") add to the documentary's high production value. And the internet rumors about Charlie Kirk being invoked in this documentary are true. I'll leave it to you as to how he comes up. DIGGER REVIEW: TOM CRUISE DESTROYS THE PLANET IN ALEJANDRO IÑÁRRITU'S GRANDIOSE, MESSY POLITICAL SATIRE CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS The Verdict: Films are a dime a dozen, but a cinematic experience is rare. "You Can See Everything" is not just a fascinating, thought-provoking documentary starring one of the 21st century's most vilified figures, it challenges the entire medium. And it's even more fun when you're able to discuss it with others after, so it's best not to go stag. Don't miss one of the biggest and best surprises of 2026 at the movies. ★★★★ — SEE IT NOW "You Can See Everything" is rated R for language and some graphic nudity. Running time: 2 hours, 54 minutes. articles.title: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026: Kylie Jenner’s $50M bra, Barbara Palvin’s postpartum return and 3 more major talking points
articles.summary: The annual lingerie show delivered plenty of memorable moments.
articles.body:
The Victoria's Secret Fashion Show returned Sunday with a star-studded spectacle. Held in Los Angeles for the first time since 2007, the annual runway show brought together Victoria's Secret veterans, including Adriana Lima and Alessandra Ambrosio, alongside newcomers Kylie Jenner, Amelia Gray Hamlin and Natalia Bryant.

There was no shortage of talking points. Bella Hadid opened the show, Rosie Huntington-Whiteley returned after 16 years, Jenner wore the Fantasy Bra and Barbara Palvin returned after welcoming her first child six weeks earlier.

Meanwhile, Megan Thee Stallion, Tate McRae, Katseye and Megan Moroney were among the performers and Nicole Kidman, Lisa Rinna, Timothée Chalamet and Dylan Sprouse were among the A-listers watching in the front row.

From a surprise Gisele Bündchen cameo to Kidman's viral reactions, here are five moments everyone's talking about.

Kylie Jenner made quite the Victoria's Secret runway debut, modeling the iconic Fantasy Bra, worth a reported $50 million . The diamond-covered design, usually worn by a Victoria's Secret veteran, hasn't appeared on the runway since 2018 and is thought to be the most expensive design to ever be worn at the show.

Created in collaboration with jewelers Jacob & Co., it features 4,410 natural diamonds with a single 75-carat yellow diamond in the center.

Jenner didn't celebrate her debut alone: While her sister Kendall Jenner, a previous Victoria's Secret Angel, was absent, Kris Jenner and Timothée Chalamet were on the front row.

A day after being spotted on crutches , Bündchen made a surprise appearance at the show in a prerecorded video message that played before Bella Hadid opened the show. Wearing pink lace lingerie and a branded robe, she asked viewers, "Are you ready for the show?"

In a second video message aired at the end of the show, Bündchen also hinted that her renewed relationship with the brand may extend beyond the cameo. "Wasn't that amazing?" she asked viewers, before adding, "You are going to be seeing more of me real soon. Ciao!"

Just six weeks after welcoming her first child with husband Dylan Sprouse, Palvin was back on the runway. The new mom walked in a pink lingerie dress while Megan Moroney sang and said backstage that life now is "a ride, like a fun one, but also scary. It's a roller coaster."

Sprouse, watching from the front row, praised his wife on his Instagram story before the event, writing, "Proud of my missus, jumping right into the vs fashion show post birth. Built different. I don't know where you find the energy but damn!"

Natalia Bryant, the daughter of late NBA legend Kobe Bryant and Vanessa Bryant, was another star who made her runway debut on Sunday night. Wearing a look from the brand's sub-label, Pink, including a hot-pink shrug, bejeweled jeans and a black bra bearing the brand's name, the model walked the catwalk as Katseye performed.

While the event marked Bryant's first Victoria's Secret runway appearance, she was already familiar with the brand having starred in a campaign in fall 2024. She's also walked for a number of prestigious fashion houses in recent years, including for Versace and Boss.

Kidman might have skipped the brand's famous pink carpet, but still managed to steal the spotlight on the front row. Wearing a pink striped tie, white shirt and black pencil skirt, the actor was seated beside Vanessa Bryant and quickly became a talking point as the live show streamed.

She was filmed dancing to Megan Thee Stallion and reacting to Tate McRae's dancers but perhaps her most talked-about moment came when models walked to Adéla's song "Nicole Kidman."

The actor was spotted burying her head in her hands and smiling as the track played — but she was already familiar with it. At the London premiere of Practical Magic 2 , Kidman revealed plans to see Adéla's Nashville show on Sept. 21. She also joined Dua Lipa, Pedro Pascal and Kristen Wiig in a video set to the track at Chanel's Paris Fashion Week show last month.

articles.standfirst: Jaime Lorente debuta como director con 'El mal hijo', una película sobre las adicciones, las relaciones familiares y las heridas que se transmiten entre generaciones
articles.summary: Jaime Lorente debuta como director con 'El mal hijo', una película sobre las adicciones, las relaciones familiares y las heridas que se transmiten entre generaciones
articles.body: Jaime Lorente se estrena como director con 'El mal hijo', una película protagonizada por Miguel Ángel Puro que aborda las adicciones, las relaciones familiares y las consecuencias que determinadas heridas pueden tener de una generación a otra. El actor de 'La casa de papel' se pone por primera vez detrás de las cámaras con una historia que conecta con algunas de sus principales inquietudes personales, mientras que Puro asume un papel protagonista en un proyecto que ambos llevaban tiempo queriendo compartir. En su conversación con MARCA, los dos hablan de la experiencia de trabajar juntos, de la importancia de la confianza en un rodaje y de los temas que atraviesan la película. También hay espacio para reflexionar sobre la masculinidad, la paternidad y el éxito profesional, además de una pregunta inevitable para Lorente, reconocido aficionado del Atlético de Madrid: ¿qué preferiría, ganar un Oscar con una película dirigida por él o que el equipo rojiblanco conquistase la Champions? El origen de 'El mal hijo' está en la novela de Salvador S. Molina. Lorente encontró en ella los elementos que buscaba para su primera película como director, aunque tuvo que adaptar la historia para trasladarla al lenguaje audiovisual. "Yo tenía muy claro qué elementos quería que estuviesen en mi ópera prima y dio la bendita casualidad que la novela tenía los mismos elementos", explica. El cineasta quería abordar las adicciones y las consecuencias que pueden tener no solo sobre quienes las sufren, sino también sobre las personas que forman parte de su entorno. "Tenía muchas ganas de contar una historia sobre la adicción, sobre los esquemas familiares que se arman para sostener a una persona que sufre esta enfermedad y sobre las consecuencias a largo plazo", señala. La película se aleja de una mirada simplista sobre sus personajes y busca mostrar las circunstancias que condicionan sus decisiones. Para Lorente, comprenderlos es fundamental para construir una historia que resulte creíble. "Sabíamos que teníamos que construir un mundo y una realidad que te pudieras creer y, para ello, había que trascender el cliché, entender estos personajes, no juzgarlos, vivirlos", afirma. La amistad entre Lorente y Puro ha sido uno de los elementos que han marcado el rodaje. Ambos llevaban tiempo queriendo trabajar juntos y, según explican, la relación personal no ha impedido que cada uno asumiera su papel dentro del proyecto. "Hemos trabajado siempre desde el respeto y la escucha. Nunca nos hemos casado con nosotros mismos, porque siempre hemos estado a favor del trabajo, de lo creativo", explica Lorente. Esa confianza también permite que los intérpretes se atrevan a proponer ideas sin temor a ser juzgados. En la conversación, se destaca la importancia de crear un espacio en el que los actores puedan explorar sus personajes y aportar su visión. Para Lorente, dirigir implica estar pendiente de los procesos de los intérpretes y entender qué necesitan en cada momento. "El trabajo de escucha, el estar siempre en el otro, te facilita muchísimo el trabajo", sostiene. "Dirigir es estar al servicio de la empatía continuamente", afirma. Y añade una reflexión sobre la relación entre la creatividad y el trato personal de algunos directores: "A mí no me sirve lo de que alguien sea un genio, pero un imbécil". La película también invita a reflexionar sobre la transmisión de determinados comportamientos entre padres e hijos. Uno de los asuntos que aborda es la masculinidad entendida desde la represión emocional y la dificultad para aceptar la vulnerabilidad. Lorente aclara que la historia no plantea que la masculinidad sea negativa en sí misma, sino que cuestiona algunas conductas que se perpetúan de generación en generación. "Creo que la falta de aceptación de la vulnerabilidad, de la sensibilidad, hace que todo se convierta en rígido y se convierta en violencia", reflexiona. Las adicciones también aparecen ligadas a una cuestión social. Lorente advierte de las dificultades económicas que pueden impedir el acceso a determinados tratamientos y recuerda que el problema afecta a todo el entorno familiar. "Hay una responsabilidad social que estamos echando a un lado para los adictos, imagínate para la familia de los adictos", afirma. La conversación también deja un momento para el fútbol. Jaime Lorente es seguidor del Atlético de Madrid y la pregunta que le plantean enfrenta dos aspiraciones muy diferentes: ganar un Oscar con una película dirigida por él o ver al equipo rojiblanco levantar la Champions. El actor reconoce que la elección no es sencilla cuando se trata de dos pasiones personales. "Que una película dirigida por mí protagonizada por Simeone ganara la Champions... me lo pones muy difícil", responde entre risas para intentar evitar mojarse. Lorente se muestra convencido de que el Atlético puede conquistar el título europeo. "Este año la final de la Champions es en el estadio del Atleti y nos vamos a llevar la Champions", asegura.

articles.title: ‘Tumbbad’ fame Sohum Shah excited for SS Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’ and Ranbir Kapoor’s ‘Ramayana’;  says he is curious about Mahesh Babu starrer
articles.summary: ‘Tumbbad’ fame actor and filmmaker Sohum Shah is specifically excited for two of the biggest projects Indian cinema has to offer in a couple of months.
articles.body: ‘Tumbbad’ fame actor and filmmaker Sohum Shah is specifically excited for two of the biggest projects Indian cinema has to offer in a couple of months. He recently expressed his enthusiasm for SS Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’ and Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana’ and shared his views on the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in filmmaking and explained why he continues to prefer practical sets and real locations for his own projects.In a conversation with Variety India, Sohum Shah said he is looking forward to watching both films, although his reasons for being excited about them are different.Sohum Shah is excited about ‘Varanasi’ and ‘Ramayana’“I am excited about ‘Varanasi’ because I really like Rajamouli sir as a filmmaker. I am excited about ‘Ramayana’ as well, but I already know the story of ‘Ramayana.’ I have watched it and read it,” he said.The actor is particularly curious about ‘Varanasi’ because he wants to discover the world Rajamouli has created and the surprises the story holds. “I don’t know what ‘Varanasi’ is about, what the surprises will be or what kind of new world he is going to show us,” he said.Speaking about ‘Ramayana’, Shah praised Ranbir Kapoor’s work and said he was interested in seeing the actor portray Lord Rama. He also mentioned that the film has been made on a large scale, with the makers aiming to reach audiences across the world.He said, “I am excited about ‘Ramayana’ because I really like Ranbir’s work, and he is playing Lord Ram in the film. We will have to see how everything turns out, but they have made the film on a very large scale. I think they want to take it to the whole world.”Sohum Shah shares his views on AI in filmmakingSohum Shah believes AI can create opportunities for people who have stories to tell but lack the resources to make a film through conventional methods. He does not see AI as a threat to cinema. Instead, he believes filmmakers should choose the tools that best suit their stories and creative vision.Sohum Shah believes storytelling matters mostShah’s own approach to filmmaking relies heavily on practical sets, real locations and prosthetics, with CGI and visual effects used only when necessary. Recalling the making of the first ‘Tumbbad’, he explained that the production created much of the film’s unsettling world through physical environments. He plans to follow a similar approach for ‘Tumbbad 2’.“Definitely, in ‘Tumbbad 2,’ we will use VFX or CGI only where it is required. Otherwise, we have shot at real locations or built sets,” he said.Shah further added that his preference for practical filmmaking does not mean he opposes technological innovation. “The medium can be anything. You can tell a story through AI, through VFX, by building sets or by going to real locations. You should use whatever works for you,” he said.Speaking about the sequel, ‘Tumbbad 2’ reprises Sohum Shah’s role as Vinayak Rao with Alia Bhatt and Nawazuddin Siddiqui joining as the new faces.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
